featureShowcases.body: The StudioDash guides cover everything from connecting your developer services to understanding revenue, monitoring your app portfolio, following website performance, and keeping your information up to date. Start with the basics or jump directly to the part of StudioDash you want to explore.

sections.heading: Start with StudioDash
paragraphs: Begin with the [StudioDash Overview](/apps/studiodash) for an introduction to the product, then explore [Features](/apps/studiodash/features) to see how StudioDash brings together the different parts of running an app portfolio.

When you're ready to connect your own services, the [Integrations](/apps/studiodash/integrations) guide explains the different types of developer, advertising, analytics, website, and search services supported by StudioDash.
bullets: Overview introduces StudioDash and what it is designed to do.
Features explores the main capabilities available across the app.
Integrations explains how external services contribute information to StudioDash.

sections.heading: Monitor Your Apps
paragraphs: The StudioDash dashboard provides a central starting point for understanding what is happening across your studio. Instead of opening several external dashboards, you can begin with a single view of the information that matters to your portfolio.
For App Store information, the dedicated App Store Analytics guide explains how StudioDash helps you follow apps, downloads, sales, ratings, reviews, and release status.
bullets: Dashboard provides an overview of your studio.
App Store Analytics helps you monitor your app portfolio.
Provider health highlights connected services that may need attention.
Historical information helps put today's performance into context.

sections.heading: Understand Your Revenue
paragraphs: Revenue can come from several places, making it difficult to understand the commercial performance of your apps from any single provider dashboard. StudioDash brings supported revenue information together so you can see the wider picture.

The Revenue Analytics guide explains how to explore revenue over time, understand different sources, compare performance, and put your results into the context of the goals you have set for your studio.
bullets: Follow combined revenue from supported sources.
Explore revenue across different reporting periods.
Understand which sources and apps contribute to your results.
Use business goals to put performance into context.

sections.heading: Follow Your Website & Search Performance
paragraphs: Your website and search visibility can play an important role in helping people discover your apps. StudioDash can bring supported website, analytics, and search information into the same workspace as your app and revenue data.
The Website & SEO Analytics guide explains how these services contribute to the wider picture of your studio's online performance.
bullets: Monitor supported website analytics.
Follow search performance and visibility.
Review website trends alongside your app portfolio.

sections.heading: Look Beyond Today's Numbers
paragraphs: StudioDash is designed to help you understand how performance changes over time rather than simply showing the latest figures. Historical information and different reporting periods provide context for changes across your apps and connected services.
The Reporting guide covers the tools available for reviewing and using this information.

sections.heading: Keep Your Information Up to Date
paragraphs: On Mac, StudioDash can keep supported provider information updated in the background, reducing the need to refresh each service manually before checking your dashboard.
The Automation & Sync guide explains background updates, manual refresh, provider health, cached information, and how StudioDash handles services that update on different schedules.
bullets: Background synchronisation on Mac.
Manual refresh when you need fresh information.
Clear provider health and update status.
Fast access to information StudioDash has already collected.

sections.heading: Understand Security & Privacy
paragraphs: StudioDash connects to services that may contain important business information, so security and privacy are an essential part of the product.
The Security & Privacy guide explains how StudioDash approaches connected accounts, credentials, permissions, and your control over the services you choose to connect.

sections.heading: Choose the StudioDash Experience You Need
paragraphs: StudioDash is designed around Free, Pro, and Studio plans so developers can choose the level of analytics and business insight that suits the way they work.

Free provides a useful starting point for monitoring your studio, while Pro and Studio provide access to additional analytics, reporting, and business capabilities. Optional cloud features can extend StudioDash further where available.

sections.heading: More StudioDash Resources
paragraphs: Additional guides provide quick answers, visual examples, and information about changes to StudioDash.
Use the FAQ when you have a specific question, browse Screenshots for a visual tour, or check Release Notes to see what has changed between versions.
